fieldValues.title: 6. Build: what we tried and where we went too far
fieldValues.thinking_reached:
The ideal: The change is made once, in the layer that owns it, in a clean workspace against the right build, and is not lost.

What we have tried: scripts/wt worktrees; pinned CLI builds and srs-pinned; the stale-sibling rule (srs-rust#874); capability layering and ADR-048; the revision-bump choreography; the MCP tool-first rule against mimicry; the release-plan practice from the RFC-051/052 retrospective.

Problems recorded here: SP-08, SP-28, SP-77, SP-30, SP-01, SP-49.
fieldValues.tensions:
- Line 2, Compatibility and a clean cut (chosen 2026-10-25: 'Prepare the workspace and ship the change' failed the coupled-cost test; stale workspaces are a problem to fix, finding 9cd7e06c): too far toward both, by turns. RFC-051 and RFC-052 took 45 PRs, 9 repositories and 9 releases over 2 days 21 hours (retrospective); hand-written client types drift.
- Model B: WG Third-party ready merged 0 of 10 in most cycles; 140 worktrees, about 115 removable; stuck claims (clerk#25, srs-rust#1264); stale binaries and sibling checkouts (srs#874). On 2026-10-25 two reports read a local srs-rust 240 commits behind.
- The stage's other two tensions stay as records under its domain, out of this map (one trade-off per stage, owner, 2026-10-25).
fieldValues.unresolved_questions:
